newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: GOLF-MCNULTY CHASES FOURTH SUCCESSIVE TITLE.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-MCNULTY CHASES FOURTH SUCCESSIVE TITLE.

text.p: Mark McNulty, enjoying a purple patch of form, will be hunting a fourth successive South African tour title when the Players' Championship begins at Durban Country Club on Thursday.
The dapper Zimbabwean moved up three places in the world rankings to 15 after his victory on Sunday in the Wild Coast Challenge.
He is a big fan of the Durban Country Club layout.
"It's a great course and, traditionally, it's always been kept in great shape. It's almost treated like a baby with the nappy put on with powder all the time," McNulty said.
"The course also suits my game, it's all about positioning from tee to green."

By modern standards Durban Country Club is a short course and needs the wind to provide bite in its teeth. The close attendance of Cyclone Gretelle in the Indian Ocean should guarantee plenty of wind -- and this will also be in McNulty's favour.

Both of McNulty's last wins -- in the South African Masters and in the Wild Coast Challenge -- required him to play skilfully in varying wind conditions and his pinpoint iron play, allied to his ability to hit low trajectory shots when required, leaves him as the man to beat this week.
McNulty's closest challengers are likely to come from defending champion Wayne Westner of South Africa and fellow Zimbabwean Tony Johnstone.

Westner is another renowned wind player and he always feels completely at home at Durban Country Club. His victory there last year plus his two South African Open wins at the same venue in 1988 and 1991 confirm his pedigree over a course rated as one of the best in Africa.
